US drying was used to replace steam cylinders during the heat-up period, while RF was integrated into subsection 11 within the falling rate period. This hybrid system using different drying technologies shows a significant reduction in energy intensity, about 19.8%, compared to conventional drying using steam cylinders, as shown in Figure 33. 43 DE-EE0009395 Figure 33. The reduction percentage in energy intensity from using of a hybrid system of steam cylinders, US and RF within the drying process (Fine paper) The new TEA approach was conducted to investigate the impact of integrating RF and US technologies on the performance of the dryer section within the paper machine. The baseline case of the industrial paper machine for linerboard production, developed and documented in the project, was considered. The dryer section of the baseline case consists of the main and after sections with eight steam groups. This baseline case can be used to compare the performance of the new configuration of the integrated hybrid drying process of RF and US at the commercial scale of the dryer section to the baseline case.
